newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agreement on food labelling law.
newsitem.headline: EU agreement on food labelling law.

text.p: The Irish presidency welcomed on Friday the agreement between the Council and the European Parliament on a new European Union directive on labelling, advertising and presentation of foodstuffs.

The directive, deadlocked for many months in conciliation negotiations before Thursday's deal, is designed to provide additional information to enable consumers to distinguish the true nature of any product as well as between products.
In addition, it would ensure that the language used on labelling is more easily understood by the consumer.

"In particular, more information must be given on the sales name of the product, its composition and ingredients, and where applicable, the presence of starches likely to contain gluten," Irish Consumer Affairs Minister Pat Rabitte said in a statement.
The EU Council of Consumer Ministers reached a political agreement on the issue already in March 1995. The new directive amends existing legislation which dates back to 1979.
"This is a significant sucess for the Irish presidency in the consumer arena," Rabitte said.
